Maria (customer-success): FYI ACME reported a sudden p99 spike on embeddings & text-gen around 09:12 UTC. They insist requests should stay in eu-west-1 but traces show lots of cross-region hops. Request-id: 01FZk9... Can someone triage?
Sam (support): Got it — can you paste one failing request-id + example client IP and region header they’re using?
Maria (customer-success): Request 01FZk9B2, client IP 34.122.11.45, they include header x-region: eu-west-1. Attached trace snippet from their SDK.
Jordan (eng-sre): I pulled logs for that request-id. Edge in eu-west-1 accepts it, but backend connection goes to 52.18.200.10 (us-east-1) before hitting our model pool. Traceroute output I grabbed: 

```
traceroute to model.internal (52.18.200.10), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.5 ms
 2  52.18.200.10  120 ms
```

Sam (support): Ouch. Who owns egress mapping / egress-proxy config for eu-west? Could be NAT or policy misconfig. :thinking:
Jordan (eng-sre): Looking at gitops, egress-proxy in eu-west had a canary PR r-3321 that updated route selectors. The selector used 'model-tier:stable' but the canary mistakenly included 'region:us' tag in the template. So failover started directing traffic to the US model pool.
Aisha (oncall): Oncall here — initiating rollback of r-3321 on egress-proxy-eu-west now.
deploy-bot: rollback r-3321 initiated, target: egress-proxy-eu-west, canary=2
Jordan (eng-sre): After rollback I re-ran traceroute from the same edge node. Now backend IP resolves to model.internal -> 172.31.40.22 (eu-west) and latency is stable ~12ms.
Sam (support): Can we add repro steps for support & CS to validate with customers? I'll paste a short checklist: 
1) curl -H "x-region: eu-west-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}' --verbose
2) capture the request-id returned and run `traceroute $(dig +short model.internal)` from an internal debug host or ask us for the trace.
Please paste both outputs.
Maria (customer-success): I sent the steps to the customer; they ran them and confirmed p99 dropped back to baseline after ~3 minutes. They shared new request-id 01FZk9C7 showing eu route.
Jordan (eng-sre): Root cause summary: mis-tagged canary introduced 'region:us' on an eu egress-proxy selector that should have been region-agnostic or explicitly eu. Result: service routing picked a us egress IP for matching model-tier label. Fixes: immediate rollback + patch to gitops validation to reject cross-region tags in egress-proxy manifests. Also adding an alert when egress IP allocation maps to a different cloud region than the edge.
Sam (support): I'll draft the customer-facing explanation and share the timeline. Also asked infra to add a short runbook for support: how to collect traceroute + env metadata.
Aisha (oncall): Incident logged as INC-2026-112. Postmortem will include remediation & prevention items.
Maria (customer-success): Thanks team :rocket: Customer is OK with the explanation and wants a short note when the guardrails are in place.
Jordan (eng-sre): Pushed unit test in gitops: manifests with egress-proxy must not contain a conflicting region tag. CI will fail on future PRs.
Sam (support): Closing the ticket from support side after I sync the remediation note with CS.
Maria (customer-success): Closing loop with ACME now, will ask for final confirmation tomorrow.
Aisha (oncall): 👍 I'll attach the network traces to the incident and schedule a 1:1 postmortem review.
